meta.purpose: Breaks the consumer PWA (Docs/22 W- screens, WP19 'Consumer PWA') into stages that can each run in a fresh context. Each stage reports back into this file, so the next context knows what is done, what changed, and what to watch out for.
how_to_use: Start a new context with: 'Run stage <id> of pwa/dev_plan.json' (ids are P1..P14; backend stages are always written 'backend S<n>' to avoid confusion).

Read this file first: global_decisions, conventions, doc_issues, backend_readiness, the reports of all completed stages, handoff_notes and open_questions. Then read only the doc sections listed in the stage's context_to_read.

Check backend readiness before a stage that depends on it: read backend/dev_plan.json meta.progress, or run `pnpm contract:coverage` in backend/. If a needed backend stage is not done, build the screens against the contract, show the 'not available yet' state for 501 responses (GD-13), and list the gap in the stage report.

Before starting, set the stage status to 'in_progress' and fill report.started_at. Update each task's status as you go (not_started | in_progress | done | deferred | blocked), so a context that runs out mid-stage can be resumed.

When finishing, fill the stage report (summary, screens_done, deviations, notes_for_next, tests_after_stage), set status to 'done' (or 'partial' with reasons), append to handoff_notes and deviations_log, update meta.progress and screen_coverage, and set meta.last_updated.
Never delete earlier reports. Correct them by appending a note that says what changed.
If a stage changes a global decision, add an amendment to that decision with the stage id and a reason. Do not edit the decision in place without a trace.

If a stage must change backend code (e.g. DI-08 storage CORS), keep the change minimal, add tests in backend/, run the backend checks, and record it in both this file (deviations_log) and backend/dev_plan.json (handoff_notes).

auth_server_facts: Client cp-web-consumer is registered: confidential, refresh 12 h idle / 7 days absolute, allowed for the authorization-code and the anonymous grant (backend/libs/auth/index.ts).
Client cp-ssr gets a public.read client-credentials token (no refresh).

auth.authorize 302s to CARPAL_SIGNIN_URL (default <issuer>/signin) with ?interaction_id=…&ui_locales=…, and sets the interaction cookie (__Host-cp_ia, SameSite=Lax, Path=/). After the hosted UI completes, the UI sends the browser back to the same /oauth/authorize URL, which redirects to redirect_uri with code and state.
Redirect URIs come from CARPAL_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URIS (JSON); the dev default for cp-web-consumer is https://carpal.app/bff/oauth/callback, so local development must override it (P2).
private_key_jwt, mTLS, DPoP-Nonce, attestation and PoW are enforced only with CARPAL_STRICT_AUTH=1 (backend GD-06). In lite/dev the BFF calls the token endpoint without client authentication.
The storage listener (:8083) sends no CORS headers, so a browser cannot PUT a signed upload cross-origin yet (DI-08).
The auth host does not check Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site on /v1/auth/* yet (DI-09).

global_decisions.decision: One Next.js app (App Router, React Server Components, TypeScript strict, ESM) in pwa/, managed by pnpm with its own lockfile (no root workspace, so backend/ stays untouched). Styling with Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first config). Exact versions are the current stable releases at P1 install time and are recorded in the P1 report.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/02 §2 names React + Next.js + Tailwind for the consumer PWA (SSR for public SEO pages). A standalone package mirrors backend/ and avoids reworking the backend's install.

global_decisions.decision: Node: the PWA runs on the project-local Node 24 that backend/ already installed. pwa/tools/use-local-node.sh and use-local-node.ps1 put backend/.tools/node first on PATH (and run backend's setup script if it is missing). pwa/.node-version = 24.21.0.
global_decisions.reason: System Node must stay 20.10 (backend environment note). One local Node for both packages avoids a second download.

global_decisions.decision: The consumer BFF (Docs/41 D4/G2, Docs/40 SEC-WEB) is built inside the PWA as server-only code (pwa/src/server/bff/) mounted by Next.js route handlers: /api/v1/[...path] (1:1 forwarder), /bff/login, /bff/oauth/callback, /bff/logout, /bff/session, /bff/csrf. The BFF code is written over standard Request/Response with no Next.js imports, so it can later move to backend/api-gateway/ unchanged.
global_decisions.reason: SEC-WEB-1/2 require a same-origin BFF that holds the tokens; backend/dev_plan.json defers BFFs to backend/api-gateway 'later' and none of backend S7-S9 builds them. Building it with the PWA is the only way to make the PWA work, and keeping it framework-free keeps the Docs/41 placement possible.

global_decisions.decision: Contract types are generated, never hand-written. pwa/tools/contract/generate.ts reads backend/libs/contract/generated/{operations.json,schemas.json,operation-schemas.json,enums.ts,errors.ts} and writes shared/api-contracts/generated/ (operation map: opId → method, path template, path params, query, input/response TypeScript types, sec tags such as IDEM/ETAG/AAL2/FLAG; enums; error codes). `pnpm contract:generate` regenerates; `pnpm contract:check` fails when stale. The PWA imports it through a linked package (@carpal/api-contracts, 'link:../shared/api-contracts').
global_decisions.reason: Docs/02 §6.1 'strict API contracts: TypeScript clients generated into shared/api-contracts; a breaking API change fails the PWA build'. The backend's OpenAPI file is a backend S9 item, but its generated registry already exists and is checked against Docs/40.

amendments.change: shared/api-contracts/openapi.yaml now exists (backend S9c, GD-37; written and checked only by backend `pnpm openapi:check`). The PWA generator still reads backend/libs/contract/generated/ (it carries the parsed sec tags the BFF allowlist needs) and writes only shared/api-contracts/generated/** and shared/api-contracts/package.json + index files; it never writes openapi.yaml. The server-defined Json<…> shapes (MatchReasonValues, FeedCard, TemplateParams, InsightPayload, SuggestionPayload, WebAuthn option/credential JSON …; backend DI-50) are taken from the OpenAPI components, so the generator reads openapi.yaml for those types only. The registry now has 406 operations / 458 routes, the {VT} dual-scope alias (vehicle transfers) and multi-route operations; the generator must emit every route of an operation with its scope (me | fleet | org).
amendments.reason: BA-24; avoids two writers of shared/api-contracts and closes the x-server-schema gap.

amendments.change: Contract types regenerated at 1.1.0 (407 operations) in P7, ahead of P14: the backend registry had changed with S10, so contract:check failed. Fixtures and the allowlist count (171 consumer + 18 fleet-driver routes, search.session_get admitted by rule (a)) follow.
amendments.reason: pnpm check must pass at every stage; P14.T1 keeps the E2E stubs and the behaviour.

global_decisions.decision: Hosted sign-in UI (Docs/40 §6.2 'hosted sign-in UI on id.carpal.app', screens of W-AUTH-01 / S-AUTH-02,03,07,08,09) is built in the PWA codebase as its own route group (/id/signin/...). Dev topology: the PWA proxies /id/oauth/*, /id/v1/auth/* and /id/.well-known/* to the auth host (127.0.0.1:8082), so the hosted UI and the auth endpoints share one origin and the interaction cookie is first-party. Backend env for dev: CARPAL_SIGNIN_URL=http://localhost:3000/id/signin and CARPAL_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URIS={"cp-web-consumer":["http://localhost:3000/bff/oauth/callback"]}. The BFF exchanges codes and refresh tokens server-to-server directly with :8082.
global_decisions.reason: The interaction cookie is set by the auth host, so the sign-in page must be on the same origin as /v1/auth/*. No sign-in UI exists in backend/. Production placement (id.carpal.app served from the PWA build, or a separate small app) is OQ-03.

amendments.change: Dev backend env (backend/.env, loaded by `pnpm dev`) also needs CARPAL_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=localhost and CARPAL_WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS=["http://localhost:3000"] (defaults are carpal.app and https origins; passkeys are now implemented, BA-09). Completion of the hosted UI re-requests the same /oauth/authorize URL (cookie-bound interaction); an unknown or expired interaction answers 410 LINK_EXPIRED, which the hosted UI turns into 'This sign-in page expired' plus a restart of /bff/login with the same return URL (BA-12). /oauth/token errors are RFC 6749 JSON (ProtocolError), not problem+json; the BFF maps both. DPoP proofs sent to /oauth/token must use htu = <issuer>/oauth/token (issuer from the discovery document), even though the BFF connects to 127.0.0.1:8082 (DI-17, GD-07 amendment).
amendments.reason: BA-09, BA-12; verified in backend/libs/config/config.ts and modules/identity/application/auth-server.ts on 2026-10-25.

amendments.change: Dev values as built: redirect URI https://localhost:3000/bff/oauth/callback (Url is https-only, DI-24), CARPAL_SIGNIN_URL=https://localhost:3000/id/signin (optional: the proxy rewrites issuer redirects to <origin>/id), CARPAL_WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS=["https://localhost:3000"]. CARPAL_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URIS replaces the whole map, so it lists the other clients' defaults too (pwa/README.md, backend/.env.example comment). The /id proxy exposes auth.authorize, auth.pow_challenge, discovery, JWKS and every /v1/auth/* operation, never /oauth/token or /oauth/revoke; it passes only the __Host-cp_ia cookie in both directions.
amendments.reason: DI-24; keeps the BFF the only token client.

amendments.change: Hosted sign-in as built: page /id/signin (root layout src/app/id/layout.tsx over the shared document src/app/root-document.tsx; language from ui_locales, set by the proxy as x-carpal-locale). Completion: the /id proxy sets __Host-cp_iar (interaction id + the authorize query, 30 min, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) when authorize answers with the sign-in page and clears it when authorize answers the client; the page re-requests that authorize URL without prompt=login (the auth host never resumes a prompt=login request, DI-34). Expired interaction (410): 'Start again' → /bff/login/restart?state=… (same return URL, level, screen, intent; pending logins are remembered 12 h for this, the callback still takes them for 30 min). What /bff/login asked to show (screen=signup, the gated action's label) is read on the server from the BFF session store by the authorize state (loginHint) — valid while the hosted UI and the BFF share origin and store; a separate id host (OQ-03) needs another carrier. Dev without TLS (OQ-10): CARPAL_PWA_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI registers the https callback and the /id proxy rewrites the auth host's redirect to it back to <origin>/bff/oauth/callback (env.ts refuses the variable in prod).
amendments.reason: P4.T1, BA-12; verified live (test:int) and in the browser (E2E).

global_decisions.decision: 'Intent survives sign-in' (Docs/22 principle 2) is done with a context modal plus a redirect, not a credentials modal: a gated action opens a small modal ('Sign in to follow Reza Auto Suspension') with Log in / Sign up; the action (type, target, return URL, form draft) is stored server-side in the BFF pre-session (TTL 30 min, size-capped), the browser goes through the hosted sign-in, and on return the page replays the action once and shows its toast.
global_decisions.reason: Credentials must be entered on the hosted sign-in origin (GD-05; frame-ancestors 'none' forbids an iframe). Logged as DI-01.

amendments.change: As built (src/components/shell/auth-intent.tsx): useGatedAction() → gate({type, target, draft, title, run}) runs the action for a signed-in user, otherwise opens the context modal (title e.g. shell.intent.follow, text, Log in / Sign up); Log in saves the intent (POST /bff/intents with CSRF) and goes to /bff/login?return_to=<this page>&locale (Sign up adds screen=signup, honoured from P4). Pages register useIntentHandler(type, intent => toast text); after sign-in the replayer consumes each pending intent whose return_to path is this page and whose handler is mounted, exactly once (consume is atomic in the BFF), shows the returned toast and refreshes the session view.
amendments.reason: P3.T5; the browser round trip through the hosted sign-in is verified in P4 (needs the hosted UI and local https, OQ-10).

amendments.change: The intent carries an optional plain-text label (≤ 160 characters: the modal's heading) and /bff/login names it (intent=<id>), so the hosted sign-in shows 'Sign in to follow Reza Auto Suspension' above the form. Every ordinary sign-in returns through /<locale>/onboarding?next=<page> (P4.T7), so a new account onboards first and the action replays when it reaches the page (the replay is unchanged). Round trip verified in the browser: dev kit Follow → Log in → hosted sign-in with the context line → onboarding 'Finish later' → back on /en/dev-kit with the toast and 'Following'.

Community intents: react.helpful / react.like (target '<type>:<id>'), comment ('<type>:<id>', draft {body}), answer (question id, draft {body}), ask (draft: title, body and the picked brand/model/series/category/symptom ids — never a garage vehicle id, which a guest does not have) and report ('<type>:<id>', draft {reason, details}). Because the registry keeps one handler per type, pages mount one handler per type (ReactionIntentHandlers, CommentIntentHandlers; ReportHost in the shell frame) that act on the target from the intent; mounted reaction buttons learn the replayed state through a listener map.

Types: settings.email_change, settings.phone_change, settings.password, settings.totp_enroll, settings.passkey, settings.mfa_remove, settings.recovery_codes, settings.sessions_revoke_all, settings.dsr_create, settings.dsr_download, settings.membership_leave. The password and passkey handlers reopen their form (no stored secret; the browser's passkey sheet needs a gesture).

Link pages that need a signed-in user (/l/ri code entry, /l/cn) do not use intents: the token stays in the tab (sessionStorage cp:link:<ri|cn>, 30 min) and the sign-in returns to /l/<type> without it.

global_decisions.decision: Tokens per audience: (a) signed-in browser sessions use the user's cp-web-consumer tokens (refresh rotated in the BFF; a refresh-reuse error ends the session); (b) guests get an anonymous cp-web-consumer token (scope 'public.read search', 15 min, no refresh) created lazily per pre-session (SEC-AU-14); (c) server rendering of public pages uses a cached cp-ssr client-credentials token (public.read). Every BFF call sends CarPal-Client 'cp-web-consumer/<version> (web 1.0)' (or cp-ssr), Accept-Language from the URL locale, and CarPal-Timezone from the browser.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 §2.2, SEC-AU-14, §1.3. If a PUB operation rejects the cp-ssr scope (e.g. search.run for directory pages), SSR falls back to an anonymous token held by the server (DI-16).

amendments.change: Correction: the cp-ssr scope question is DI-14 (the 'DI-16' in the reason above is a typo). Anonymous tokens are DPoP-bound by the BFF: each pre-session holds its own ES256 key pair (server-side, in the session record) and every anonymous grant for that pre-session carries a DPoP proof made with it, so the backend's anonymous key (HMAC of cnf.jkt) stays the same across the 15-minute renewals. Without a proof the auth server gives every anonymous token a new random subject, so a guest's search sessions (search.page / search.refine), match sessions and rate-limit attribution would be lost at each renewal (DI-17). In lite mode the API does not check the binding; in strict mode the BFF adds a DPoP proof (htu = API URL, ath) to every API call made with a bound token. The token client takes a pluggable client-authentication strategy (none in lite; private_key_jwt over mTLS for cp-web-consumer and cp-ssr in strict mode, backend NI-01) and a PoW hook for the ATT anonymous grant in strict mode (DI-22).
amendments.reason: DI-17, DI-22, BA-26; verified in backend modules/identity/application/auth-ops.ts (#anonymous: subject uuidv7 unless DPoP) and libs/auth/authenticator.ts (anonKey from cnf.jkt ?? sub).

amendments.change: As built: SessionTokens (user refresh single-flight per session; anonymous grant per pre-session with one ES256 key in the session record) and SsrTokens (cp-ssr cached until 30 s before expiry; anonymous fallback with a process-wide key). The SSR fallback trigger is a 401 that persists after one fresh cp-ssr token. CarPal-Client always names the token's client (cp-ssr for cp-ssr tokens). Strict seams: ClientAuthentication (none | privateKeyJwt), DPoP proofs on API calls for bound tokens (htu = CARPAL_API_AUDIENCE + path), DPoP-Nonce retry at /oauth/token, PoW hook (CARPAL_STRICT_AUTH=1 = up front).

global_decisions.decision: BFF session store behind a port: lite = in-memory Map with TTL (single process, dev); full = Redis adapter (written, not verified, like the backend's full mode). Session cookie __Host-cp_sid (Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/), 256-bit random id, holds nothing but the id. CSRF: synchronizer token bound to the session, sent as X-CSRF-Token by the typed client on every non-GET call, plus Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin and Origin == app origin checks (SEC-WEB-3). The forwarder only allows the consumer audience from the generated registry (USR/PUB operations on the api host; no {org}, {adm} or fleet-manager paths) (SEC-WEB-5), strips cookies and browser-only headers, and passes CarPal-Retry-After-Ms / CarPal-Poll-After-Ms / retry_after_ms through unchanged (SEC-RL-5).
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 SEC-WEB-1..5, SEC-RL-5. The browser on http://localhost accepts Secure cookies (localhost is a secure context).

amendments.change: Allowlist rule made precise: the forwarder admits a route when it is on the api host and either (a) it has no {org_id} path parameter and one of its principal alternatives contains USR, PUB or LNK (160 operations), or (b) it is a /v1/orgs/{org_id}/fleet/… route whose principal alternatives contain DRV (18 operations: vehicles.list/get/mileage_add/mileage_list/status_history, issues.create/list/get/update, reminders.list, service_records.list/get, appointments.list/get/history/notes_list/check_in/delay) — fleet drivers use the consumer PWA (P12) and the backend checks the assignment per request (SEC-AZ-7, backend GD-20/GD-38). Auth-host operations are never forwarded by /api/v1 (they go through the /id proxy of GD-05). Media operations on single paths (USR | ORG(ANY)) fall under (a).
amendments.reason: BA-22; without (b) the P12 driver views could not reach their routes.

amendments.change: As built: 161 consumer routes + 18 DRV fleet routes are admitted (the '160 operations' of the alignment counted operations; one operation has two qualifying routes). Paths must be canonical (no dot segments, empty segments, encoded slashes/backslashes or non-ASCII); HEAD/OPTIONS are 405. Safe requests with Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site or same-site are refused too. The session record holds user tokens, the anonymous token, the DPoP key, pending logins (≤ 5, 30 min), intents (≤ 5, 30 min, ≤ 8 KiB) and a profile (display name from me.get); it is created lazily by /bff/csrf, /bff/login and the first /api/v1 call — /bff/session and SSR never create one. Updates are serialized per session id inside the process. The Redis adapter uses a built-in RESP2 client (no dependency), unverified.

One pre-session per page: when a page's first API call and its first /bff/csrf ran at the same time without a session cookie, the BFF created two pre-sessions and the later Set-Cookie orphaned the other's intents and pending sign-ins (found by the gated-action E2E). The browser now creates the pre-session through one shared /bff/csrf (sharedCsrfSource, used by the typed client and the session helpers) before any api-host call; server-side creation stays as it was (DI-36). Session record additions: persistent=false when 'Keep me signed in' is off (cp_keep=0 set by the hosted sign-in, read and cleared by the callback: browser-session cookie, absolute expiry ≤ one idle period); PendingLogin gains screen, prompt and intentId; PendingIntent gains label. Step-up check in the callback: the new authentication must be fresh (auth_time ≥ start − 5 s); aal3 needs the level, aal2 is met by a fresh sign-in of an account without a second factor (BA-11; the old acr-only check refused those).

Allowlist rule (a) corrected: a route is a consumer route when it is outside the organization scope /v1/orgs/{org_id}/… and admits USR, PUB or LNK — not when it merely has an {org_id} parameter. Newly admitted: follows.put/delete, favorites.put/delete, public.org_reviews, public.org_portfolio, public.org_inventory_search, public.availability, posts.public_list (170 consumer + 18 fleet-driver routes).
amendments.reason: DI-40; found by the P5 Follow round trip (the BFF answered 404).

amendments.change: The forwarder refreshes the session record's profile (display name, locale) from successful GET/PATCH /v1/me responses, so /bff/session (the header's name) follows a profile edit without a new sign-in.

global_decisions.decision: Data access: server components call the backend through a server-side typed client (same generated operation map) for public reads; client components use TanStack Query over the browser-side typed client that calls the BFF (/api/v1/...). The typed client adds Idempotency-Key (UUIDv7, kept across automatic retries) for IDEM operations and If-Match from the last ETag for ETAG operations, maps problem+json to typed errors (code catalog from the registry), and implements SEC-RL-4 once: honour retry/poll delays + 0-20 % jitter; otherwise exponential backoff with full jitter (base 500 ms, cap 30 s, 5 attempts) for safe methods and IDEM requests only; pause an operation after 3 consecutive 503s.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 §2.7 and §2.8 are client obligations 'enforced by contract tests'; centralizing them avoids every screen re-implementing them.

amendments.change: (1) ApiProblem carries the optional Problem members of Docs/40 §4.2: errors (FieldError list), requirements, consent_type, entitlement_key, safety (SafetyBlock & do_not_drive), fallback_path, vin_transfer_available (BA-03). (2) ETags are read from the ETag response header, never derived from a body version (questions carry no version in the body, backend DI-47); onboarding.update sends If-Match "v1" when no ETag is known for the flow (backend DI-14). (3) Automatic retries only when the server delay is ≤ 30 s; longer delays (e.g. the 3600 s of the appointment request caps, backend DI-55) are surfaced to the screen as a typed RateLimited error with the time, never slept on. (4) 400 CURSOR_MISMATCH on a page request means the cursor is no longer valid for this caller (e.g. a guest whose pre-session expired): the client re-runs the first page instead of showing an error. (5) A 412 VERSION_MISMATCH on a user edit becomes 'This changed elsewhere — reload' without losing input; reactions bump the version of posts and answers (backend S6), so the client refreshes the cached ETag after a reaction.

As built in src/lib/api/: createApiClient({ transport }) with api() (data) and call() (data + status, etag, pollAfterMs, replayed, requestId); browser transport to /api (api host) and /id (auth host); route choice by org_id; ApiProblem with every Problem member plus stepUp from WWW-Authenticate; automatic retries on 429/502/503/504 and network errors only (not 500, never AI_UNAVAILABLE); PAUSED after 3 consecutive 503s; CarPal-Poll-After-Ms pacing per operation+path; PoW on ATTESTATION_REQUIRED for the ATT operations; CURSOR_MISMATCH restart in useApiInfiniteQuery.

Writes on items read from a list (reminders, documents) send If-Match from the ETag cache when the item’s own path was read, else "v<version>" — the backend’s ETag form (SEC-IC-3, backend libs/concurrency formatEtag). The amendment-2 rule (ETag header first) still holds: list responses carry no per-item ETag header.
amendments.reason: P7; ETAG operations answer 428 without If-Match.

global_decisions.decision: i18n: i18next + react-i18next. Dictionaries live in shared/i18n/locales/{en,fa}.json (nested keys, namespaced per area) and are bundled into the PWA as the fallback; at runtime the PWA may fetch a newer version from config.client i18n.base_url/version and cache it. `pnpm i18n:check` fails if any en key is missing in fa (Docs/02 §3.1). Locale is the first URL segment (/fa, /en; default from region config = fa); <html lang dir> are set on the server. Dates use Intl with calendar 'persian' for fa (Jalali) and gregorian for en; digits follow the UI language (Intl 'fa' → Persian digits); plates, phones, codes and URLs stay as typed and are isolated with <bdi>. No date library unless Intl falls short (record it if added).
global_decisions.reason: Docs/02 §3.1-3.4, design system 'Bidirectional layout' and 'Content fundamentals'.

amendments.change: As built: i18next 26.4.3 + react-i18next 17.0.16. Keys are "<namespace>.<path>"; namespaces common, shell, states, system, consent, format, vehicle (165 keys). src/lib/i18n/core.ts builds an instance from given resources only; the server (src/server/i18n.ts serverI18n(locale)) uses the bundled dictionary, laid over by <i18n.base_url>/<version>/<locale>.json when config.client announces another version (https bases only; versions "dev" and "bundled" skip; 3 s timeout, 512 KiB cap, merge never removes keys, 5 min failure backoff); the [locale] layout passes only CLIENT_NAMESPACES to <I18nProvider>, feature areas add theirs with <I18nNamespaces>, so the client bundle carries no dictionary. Counts use {{count, number}} (i18next number formatter → Persian digits in fa; i18n:check accepts format suffixes). Formatting in src/lib/format (Intl only, no date library): Jalali via fa-IR-u-ca-persian, 24 h in fa, "آبان ۱۴۰۵" month order, calendar dates without zone shifts, relative time, IRR in toman, "about x km", <Bidi>; createFormatter()/useFormat(); time zone from the browser (cp_tz cookie) with Asia/Tehran until known.

OQ-11 and OQ-13 answers: (1) prices are based in USD; each browser may convert them to toman or rial at a rate it enters (Settings → On this device: rate, unit, 'Convert USD prices with this rate'); the choice lives in the cp_price cookie ('<0|1>.<toman|rial>.<rate>') so server and client render the same text; formatMoney/useFormat().money take it (USD → '$12.5' / '۱۲٫۵ دلار' unconverted; IRR amounts follow the chosen unit). (2) The time zone stays the browser's (cp_tz); until it is known the deployment's CARPAL_PWA_DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE (default Asia/Tehran, validated as an IANA zone) — the onboarding also writes the browser's zone to the account (me.update timezone). New namespaces auth, onboarding, settings (402 keys in all); {{n, number}} in the code-box labels keeps Persian digits.

New namespaces notifications (a client namespace now: the header bell renders the texts on every page), activity, and a full settings namespace (2227 keys in all). Notification texts are dictionary entries notifications.templates.<template_key>.title|text with enumerated params as notifications.values.<param>.<value>. The account preferences calendar_system, digit_style and distance_unit are saved but the web formatters keep following the page language and the region's unit (OQ-24).

New namespace reviews (link pages load it with appointments and media; the review page with profiles and media; the public profiles get only profiles.reviews.write / profiles.intent.review, so SEO pages do not ship the reviews dictionary). 2933 keys in all. Retired: activity.reviews.*, appointments.action.canReview, activity.inquiry.canReview.

global_decisions.decision: Design system: pwa/tools/sync-design-system.mjs copies tokens.css, tokens.json, fonts/ and components/bundle.css from Docs/carpal-design-system/ into shared/design-system/web/ (with --check for CI); Docs stays the source of truth. Tailwind's @theme maps the semantic tokens (ink, surface, accent, signal, border-inactive, space-*, radius-*, control-md, tap-min …); no raw hex or px values outside the token file. The design-system components (Button, Icon, TextField, Chip, Badge, Avatar, PostCard, Tagged, TopBar, TabBar, fmt) are ported as typed React components under pwa/src/components/ds/, keeping the class names and props of components/index.d.ts. Themes light | sun | dark via data-theme on <html>; sun follows prefers-contrast: more, dark follows prefers-color-scheme, both overridable in settings.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/carpal-design-system/CLAUDE.md (Web section) and README. Tailwind is kept for layout only, because Docs/02 names it; components keep the system's own CSS classes.

amendments.change: The PWA needs what mobile/preview already had to add to the design system (DI-21): the extra icons of mobile/preview/js/kit.js EX (close, down, up, calendar, clock, camera, video, image, doc, shield, info, help, lock, eye, phone, globe, spark, download, trash, edit, flag, filter, sliders, map, list, logout, refresh, offline, scan, gauge, bookmark, thumb, truck, copy, send …; send and logout mirror in RTL), Chip iconEnd, TextField end/prefix slots, the urgency colour mapping (safety-critical = danger edge + icon; urgent = signal fill; soon = signal-soft; not urgent = success outline; always icon + word), the outlined safety banner (no on-danger token), and the invisible ::after extension of 40 px controls to the 48 px tap-min. P3 ports them from kit.js into ds/ with the same names and marks them 'proposed DS addition' in a comment; the tokens stay untouched (no new hex values). shared/design-system/web/ also receives the two WOFF2 fonts and their licence files.
amendments.reason: DI-21; keeps web and the native preview on one vocabulary.

amendments.change: Delivery and Tailwind mapping as built: the browser loads /ds/tokens.css and /ds/components/bundle.css as static same-origin stylesheets (copied from shared/design-system/web into the gitignored public/ds by `node tools/sync-design-system.mjs --public`, run by `pnpm dev`/`pnpm build`), and the layout preloads only /ds/fonts/<current language face>.woff2. src/app/globals.css resets Tailwind's colour, spacing, radius, shadow, font, text, container and breakpoint scales and maps tokens with @theme inline: colours by semantic name (bg-surface, text-ink, border-border-inactive …), spacing 1-6/8/12 = --space-*, plus tap, control, control-sm, icon, avatar, bar; max-w-measure; rounded-ds-sm/md/lg/pill, shadow-ds-1/2/signal/focus, font-latin/font-persian (prefixed because e.g. --radius-md: var(--radius-md) would be self-referencing); breakpoints md 768 px and xl 1200 px.
amendments.reason: Keeps tokens.css byte-identical to Docs, gives the font a stable preload URL, and makes non-token utilities impossible rather than just discouraged.

amendments.change: As built: src/components/ds/ ports Button (+ buttonClass for links), Icon (21 core + 47 kit.js glyphs; mirrors back/next/arrow/chat/comment/send/logout), TextField (prefix/end), Chip (iconEnd, toggle=false, label, disabled), Badge, Avatar, Tagged, PostCard (optional on* handlers), TopBar, TabBar (items may carry href + linkAs for real navigation), fmt, plus proposed additions IconButton (count/dot), Banner/SafetyBanner (outlined) and Urgency. Avatar sizes snap to 24/32/40/44/48/64/96 through classes because the CSP forbids inline styles. CSS: /ds/components/bundle.css is unlayered, so additions.css and shell.css are unlayered too and refine DS classes with compound selectors (.cp-iconbtn.pwa-…) — a rule in @layer components can never override bundle.css. Themes: automatic (no cookie: prefers-contrast more → sun, prefers-color-scheme dark → dark, else light) or a stored choice; a nonce'd boot script sets data-theme before paint; the picker is a set of ?theme= links (works without JavaScript, instant once hydrated).

global_decisions.decision: Map: MapLibre GL JS, loaded with a dynamic import only on W-MAP-01, the W-SRCH-01 map pane and on click elsewhere (profiles show a static preview first). Style URL from config.client region.map.style_url, overridable by the PWA env CARPAL_PWA_MAP_STYLE_URL. When no style is reachable (the pilot URLs are placeholders today), the map renders a built-in minimal style (plain background, no basemap) so pins, clusters, list sync and keyboard control still work, with the '© OpenStreetMap contributors' attribution always shown. No public OSM tile servers in committed config.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/02 §2 (MapLibre, own tiles, public OSM servers not used), Docs/22 W-MAP-01 'map code loads only on this page', shared/region-config/ir-pilot.json placeholders. Tile source is OQ-02.

amendments.change: As built: maplibre-gl 6.14.0, dynamic import (features/map/maplibre.ts); the worker URL is a bundler asset under /_next/static/media/ (admitted by the Trusted Types default policy and worker-src 'self' — no named policy, no blob:); MapLibre's CSS replaced by a few rules in map.css; no MapLibre controls/popups (innerHTML). The page CSP admits the origins of CARPAL_PWA_MAP_STYLE_URL and the pilot region file's style_url and tiles_url (src/server/map-config.ts); pages pass mapStyleUrl(region) (null unless allowed); the client tries the style once per tab (4 s, failure remembered 10 min) and otherwise draws the built-in style (background + radius layers). Pins and clusters are DOM markers (React portals) in list order; clusters come from map.pins.
amendments.reason: P6.T3; Trusted Types and CSP verified in the production build (E2E).

global_decisions.decision: Graceful degradation is part of every screen: 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED (backend not there yet), 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE, flags off in config.client (map.enabled, qna.enabled, community.*, ai.*, featured.enabled), 404 (never 403, SEC-AZ-2) and 410 each map to a defined UI state from Docs/21/22 ('not available yet', AI-off fallback, no access, removed). A screen never crashes or loops on them.
global_decisions.reason: The backend is mid-build (backend_readiness); Docs/40 SEC-AI-6 requires search, profiles and appointments to keep working without AI.

amendments.change: Re-weighted: 501 now only comes from auth.social_start (post-MVP, never called) and stays a defensive state. The degradations that will really happen are: (a) AI 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE — staging/prod run CARPAL_MCP_MODE=unavailable until the real MCP gateway exists (backend GD-35, NI-09), so the AI-off path is the expected pilot state, not an edge case; dev defaults to the deterministic stub; E2E covers both by starting the backend with CARPAL_MCP_MODE=unavailable for the AI-off suite; the triage 503 body carries safety and fallback_path (BA-02); (b) flags off by default in the seeds: community.feed.enabled, community.comments.enabled and qna.enabled are false (Should-have), featured.enabled false, map.enabled and the ai.* flags true (DI-18); (c) moderation holds: community text and Path 1 reviews with links, emails or phone numbers are held for the moderation queue (backend GD-22) and public media stay private until moderated, so 'Being reviewed' and media placeholders are normal states.

As built (src/components/shell/states.tsx): StateView kinds notAvailable, featureOff, aiOff, noAccess, removed, beingReviewed, notFound, error, offline, rateLimited, empty (icon + title + text + one action; takes t so server and client render it); stateFromProblem(): 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE → aiOff, FEATURE_DISABLED → featureOff, 501 → notAvailable, 410/LINK_* → removed, 404 → notFound, NETWORK → offline, 429/PAUSED → rateLimited, else error. ErrorBoundary/ErrorState (Retry resets TanStack queries) and app/[locale]/error.tsx (Next.js 16 passes retry). Flags: useFlag() treats unknown flags as off; when config.client is unreachable the region file is used with every flag off.

The community flags can now be switched in development (backend `pnpm dev:flags set community on`, DI-18). Flag-off states as built: Q&A pages and the ask page show featureOff (noindex), comments render nothing, followed-shop updates are hidden from Discover (the rest of Discover has no flag). Moderation holds are inferred: text matching the backend's contact-data rule is warned about before sending and shown as 'Being reviewed — only you can see this' to its author; a held question is a 404 for others (only its author reads it), so the ask page shows the held confirmation in place instead of navigating.
amendments.reason: P8; DI-50 (no moderation_status in the reads).

amendments.change: Help Me AI off as built: ai.triage.enabled off in config.client → no triage call, safety.check on the text, the Safety step with "Guided help is temporarily unavailable", then the category picker (top-level service systems) and a Help Me search; 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE from triage.start/reply (flag on, MCP off) → the same path keeping Problem.safety. Low confidence (no likely system) → "General inspection recommended". Requests without triage reach the shop as "Triage: not provided".

global_decisions.decision: Page URLs follow Docs/22 §6 except that they never carry free search text, coordinates, emails, phones, VINs or link tokens in the path or query (TR-7 spirit). Search pages are /<locale>/search/<search_session_id> plus enumerated filter params; the query text lives in the search session. Link tokens arrive in the fragment (/l/<type>#<token>, SEC-LT-2) and are POSTed. Help Me uses /<locale>/help/<session_id>/<step>.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 TR-7 and SEC-LT-2 vs. Docs/22 '/fa/search?…' (DI-05).

amendments.change: The header search hands its query to the search page without the URL: savePendingSearch() writes {text, node?, at} to sessionStorage "cp:pending-search" and navigates to /<locale>/search (placeholder until P6, which runs search.run and moves to /<locale>/search/<session_id>).

PendingSearch gains vehicle? {brand_node_id, model_node_id?, series_node_id?} (a guest's Your car from the landing hero, sent as filters, BA-16) and city? (region city_key → chosen_city). Profile pages read sessionStorage "cp:search-origin" {orgId, sessionId, resultId, at} for DI-10; request links carry only ids and an ISO slot time (/<locale>/help?provider&location&slot).

As built: /<locale>/search (hand-over and entry) → /<locale>/search/<session_id>?mode&sort&city&vf&km&rating&verified&open&avail&price&mobile&warranty&ev&fleet&stock&cond&delivery&sys&cat&brand&model&series&year (features/search/request.ts; unknown or malformed values dropped). Text, the user's position and map areas stay in the session and in sessionStorage cp:search:<session_id> (the stored request, ≤ 30 per tab); recent searches in localStorage cp:recent-searches. PendingSearch gains entry 'home'; window event carpal:pending-search tells an open search page about a new hand-over. Map URLs: /<locale>/map?session=<id> | ?org=<slug>&place=<location_id> | ?city=<key>; directory URLs /<locale>/<city>/<category>[/<brand>][?series=<slug>].

Help Me as built: /<locale>/help (landing; the hand-over of ?provider&location&slot&shop&via, ?vehicle&issue, ?urgent=1) and /<locale>/help/<case>/<step>, where <case> is this browser's case id (features/help/store.ts, localStorage cp:help:cases:<user id>) holding the triage session id, not the triage session id itself (DI-62). Request links gain shop=<slug> (the request step reads public.org_get by slug, DI-60) and via=profile|search|saved (the appointment source). No text in any of these URLs.

Review URLs: /<locale>/review/<slug>[?as=vendor&appointment|inquiry|record=<id>&invite=1&edit=<review id>] (ids only; Docs/22's /review/<token> is not used — the token stays in the /l/ri fragment and the invitation grant in sessionStorage cp:review-grant until its 30-minute expiry). My Activity: /<locale>/activity?tab=reviews[&review=<id>] (review notifications open it).
amendments.reason: P11.T1/T2; acceptance criterion 2 (link tokens never in a URL path, query or server log).

global_decisions.decision: Security of pages: nonce-based CSP set in Next.js middleware (script-src 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; img-src self + media host + tile host; connect-src self + tile host), Trusted Types required, COOP/CORP same-origin, Permissions-Policy (geolocation=(self), camera=(self), others off), Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, HSTS in prod. All API text renders as text: dangerouslySetInnerHTML is banned by lint (except the JSON-LD script, built with a serializer that escapes '<'). Private pages send Cache-Control: no-store and robots noindex.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 SEC-WEB-4, SEC-IN-5, Docs/22 §6 (private pages never indexed).

amendments.change: As built (src/server/security-headers.ts via src/proxy.ts): script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-…' (no 'unsafe-inline'); img/media/connect-src add the storage origin and the map style origin; worker-src 'self'; frame-src, object-src, base-uri, frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'; require-trusted-types-for 'script' with policies nextjs and nextjs#bundler in production only (dev adds 'unsafe-eval' and ws:); upgrade-insecure-requests and HSTS only on https (HSTS in prod). Private pages = /<locale>/{home,garage,help,appointments,review,settings,notifications,saved,activity}…, /id/*, /l/* → Cache-Control private, no-store + X-Robots-Tag noindex, nofollow. BFF responses carry no-store, nosniff, CORP same-origin and a sandbox CSP.
amendments.reason: P2.T8; verified in a production build with Playwright.

amendments.change: Trusted Types fix: Next.js 16.4.3's Turbopack runtime creates no policy (lazy chunks via script.src, React creates <script> elements through innerHTML, the error UI writes CSS text through innerHTML), so under the enforced CSP any lazily loaded chunk — e.g. the error boundary on a slow first response — blanked the page. The boot script now installs a "default" policy (TRUSTED_TYPES_POLICIES = nextjs, nextjs#bundler, default): script URLs only same-origin under /_next/static/ and returned unchanged (Turbopack finds its chunk scripts by the src attribute), HTML only "<script></script>" or text without "<". The boot script is the only inline script (constant, nonce'd; lint exception for its file). System pages: forbidden() (403, experimental.authInterrupts) and notFound(); 410/503 through the proxy status rewrite (src/server/system-status.ts) with no-store and noindex.
amendments.reason: P3.T3/T8; verified in production builds with Playwright (cold and warm loads).

amendments.change: Private sections now also include /<locale>/onboarding, /<locale>/login and /<locale>/signup; /id and /l pages carry Referrer-Policy no-referrer in their metadata (link tokens live in the fragment and are removed from the address bar on first read). The hosted sign-in, link pages and onboarding render without the app shell in a FlowFrame (word mark, language links, centred card) and pass axe in EN and FA.

JSON-LD (src/server/ssr/seo/json-ld.tsx) is the only other inline markup: serialized with <, >, & and U+2028/2029 escaped (so it holds no '<' and passes the Trusted Types default policy on client renders) and carrying the request nonce, so every server-sent script tag has one. Public pages are indexable (robots index, follow) with canonical and hreflang; robots.txt (request time) disallows /api, /bff, /id, /l and the private sections; images of the media host need no extra CSP entry (the storage origin is in img-src since P2). No console error or CSP violation on the provider page in a production build (E2E).

frame-src blob: on /<locale>/garage/* only (framesDocuments() in security-headers.ts; every other page keeps frame-src none): the in-place PDF preview frames a blob of the document, which the storage host serves as an attachment. The storage origin was already in img-src/media-src/connect-src (P2).
amendments.reason: P7.T4 in-place PDF preview; verified in the production build by the garage E2E (no CSP violation).

global_decisions.decision: Tests: Vitest + Testing Library (jsdom) for units and components (*.test.ts[x] next to the code); BFF integration tests (*.int.test.ts) run the BFF handlers against the live backend in lite mode; Playwright E2E (tests/e2e/) runs the built PWA against `pnpm dev` in backend/, Chromium only for now, with @axe-core/playwright on every visited page. E2E users sign up through the real hosted sign-in; one-time codes and email links are read from backend/.data/outbox-*.jsonl by a test helper (dev only). Tests use fresh emails under @test.carpal.app and assert only on their own data.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/02 WP19 tests (Playwright, RTL, accessibility); mirrors backend GD-13 (shared DB, own rows).

amendments.change: Browser sign-in in E2E without TLS: playwright.config.ts sets CARPAL_PWA_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI=https://localhost:3100/bff/oauth/callback (the backend must list it, pwa/README.md); tests/e2e/accounts.ts holds the outbox reader (readMail/mailedCode/mailedLinkToken, polling backend/.data/outbox-mail.jsonl for mails after a given time) and the user factory (createUser: a verified account with a password, made directly on the auth host). Specs that need the backend skip themselves when it is down. Fresh VINs per run (one owner per VIN, BA-04).

tests/support/totp.ts (RFC 6238) makes authenticator codes for the integration test and tests/e2e/account.spec.ts (wait for the next 30-second window before a second code). tests/setup/dom.ts sets Testing Library's asyncUtilTimeout to 5 s (findBy/waitFor), since whole-screen DOM tests can pass 1 s under full parallel load.

global_decisions.decision: Analytics: a small client queue batches registered events (search, map, directions, funnel; Docs/52 §18 names only) and sends them to events.ingest with platform 'web_pwa' (≤ 50 per request, on an interval and on visibilitychange). No personal data in properties. Cookie consent (Docs/22 §2.5) gates non-essential events. While the backend answers 501 (until backend S8), the queue drops events silently.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 §22.2 events.ingest, MVP §16 metrics, Docs/22 cookie consent.

amendments.change: events.ingest is implemented (backend S8, GD-28). The accepted event names and property vocabularies are the backend registry CLIENT_EVENTS in backend/modules/analytics/domain/events.ts (map.opened, map.pin_selected, map.vehicle_filter_toggled, map.directions_tapped, search.started, search.safety_banner_shown, search.chip_edited, search.result_opened, profile.viewed, app.opened, onboarding.step_completed); an unknown name or property makes the backend drop that event. The PWA keeps a typed copy of the registry and a unit test that reads the backend file and fails when a PWA event name or property is not registered (drift check). Contact/Call reveal has no registered event (DI-10): it sends search.result_event 'selected' when opened from a search result, otherwise nothing.

Queue skeleton as built (src/lib/analytics/): events.ts is the typed copy of CLIENT_EVENTS with the backend's value rules (events.test.ts imports backend/modules/analytics/domain/events.ts and fails on any difference); queue.ts stamps occurred_at at capture, keeps events only while consent allows analytics, sends ≤ 50 per events.ingest call (platform web_pwa, app_version from package.json) every 15 s, when full and on visibilitychange, drops > 7-day-old events, turns itself off on 501, drops 4xx-refused batches, keeps events on network errors (≤ 200). Consent: cp_consent cookie "v1.a0|a1", 180 days; no cookie = not asked = no analytics. No screen calls track() yet (P5/P6).

Events now sent: search.started (entry_point search | home | map; help_me_used false), search.chip_edited (chip_type = chip kind), search.safety_banner_shown (once per session), search.result_opened (target_type, rank), map.opened (entry_point search | profile | map), map.pin_selected (target_type location, rank), map.vehicle_filter_toggled (enabled, show_all_nearby), map.directions_tapped (navigation_app_key incl. 'device', target_type location).
amendments.reason: P6; names and values from CLIENT_EVENTS only (BA-20).

folder_layout.pwa/package.json, next.config.ts, tsconf: Package root. Scripts listed in commands_expected.
folder_layout.pwa/src/app/[locale]/(public)/: SSR public pages: landing, shop/<slug>, parts-seller/<slug>, parts/<vendor>/<item>, post/<id>-<slug>, questions, <city>/<category>[/<brand>], member/<id> (if ever enabled), map, search.
folder_layout.pwa/src/app/[locale]/(app)/: Signed-in tools: home, garage, help, appointments, review, settings, notifications, saved, activity. Layout checks the BFF session and redirects to sign-in with the return URL.
folder_layout.pwa/src/app/id/: Hosted sign-in UI (GD-05): signin, signup, verify, reset, mfa, locked. Its own minimal layout, no app shell.
folder_layout.pwa/src/app/l/[type]/: Link-token landing pages (ri, ci, ev, pr, cn): read the fragment on the client, POST it.
folder_layout.pwa/src/server/bff/: session store port + lite/redis adapters, oauth (PKCE, state, nonce, code exchange, refresh rotation, logout/revoke), forwarder (allowlist from the registry, header hygiene), csrf, pending-intent store, token providers (user, anonymous, cp-ssr). No Next.js imports.
folder_layout.pwa/src/server/ssr/: Server-side typed client and cached public reads for RSC pages; SEO helpers (metadata, hreflang, canonical, JSON-LD builders, sitemap).
folder_layout.pwa/src/lib/api/: Typed client over the generated operation map; errors; retry/backoff; idempotency; ETag cache; TanStack Query helpers.
folder_layout.pwa/src/lib/{i18n,format,config,analytic: i18next setup and loaders; Jalali dates, digits, currency, distance; config.client and taxonomy cache; event queue; directions links from region config.
folder_layout.pwa/src/components/shell/: Global header, left navigation, right rail, bottom tab bar, auth-intent modal, toasts with Undo, modal-with-URL, cookie banner, system pages.
folder_layout.pwa/src/features/<area>/: One folder per area (auth, onboarding, profiles, search, map, garage, media, community, notifications, settings, activity, help, appointments, reviews, fleet-driver, pwa): components, hooks, view models, tests.
folder_layout.pwa/tests/e2e/: Playwright specs and helpers (outbox reader, user factory).
folder_layout.shared/api-contracts/: @carpal/api-contracts: generated TypeScript from the backend registry (GD-04). Never edited by hand.
folder_layout.shared/i18n/: @carpal/i18n: locales/en.json, locales/fa.json (shared with mobile and portals later).
folder_layout.shared/design-system/web/: Synced copy of the design-system tokens, fonts and component CSS (GD-11).

conventions.naming: Screens are named by their Docs/22 id in a comment at the top of the page file (e.g. // W-GAR-01 My Garage (mirrors C-GARAGE-01/02/06/08/09)). API calls are made by operation id: api('vehicles.list', { query }) — never by hand-written paths.
ui_rules: Logical properties only (start/end, ms-/me-/ps-/pe-/start-/end-); lint forbids left/right utilities and properties.
User text: dir='auto' + unicode-bidi: plaintext; names, plates, numbers inside sentences in <bdi>.
Touch targets ≥ 48 px (tap-min); body 17 px; nothing under 13 px or weight 400.
Every icon-only button has an accessible label in the UI language; keyboard: '/' focuses search, Esc closes modals, visible focus ring (ring-focus).
Same trust language as mobile: badges, Verified visit / Approved by the business and CarPal labels, match reasons, AI suggestion labels (Docs/21 §2.3).
No Featured blocks rendered while featured.enabled is off; never on the map.
Copy: take EN/FA strings from mobile/preview/js/screens-*.js where a screen mirrors a mobile one; put them in shared/i18n under the area's namespace.
definition_of_done_per_screen: Route, layout per breakpoint (<768, 768-1199, ≥1200) and the elements of its Docs/22 entry (plus the Docs/21 element list for mirrored tools).
Every state listed in Docs/22/21 for the screen (loading skeleton, empty, error with Retry, 404/410, no access, 501/AI-off per GD-13).
EN and FA with correct direction; Daylight, Sunlight and Night themes.
Data only through the typed client; IDEM/ETAG handled by the client; gated actions go through the auth-intent modal (GD-06).
SEO for public pages (title, description, canonical, hreflang, JSON-LD, preview image, index/noindex per Docs/22 §6); no-store and noindex for private pages.
Tests: component tests for the view model/states; at least one Playwright path through the screen in EN or FA with an axe check (the key-flow E2E suites come in P13).

commands_expected.lint: pnpm lint (ESLint incl. RTL/logical-property and no-dangerouslySetInnerHTML rules)
